**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam).

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** When finding an empirical formula, after converting each element's mass to moles, you should next:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ divide every element's moles by the molar mass of the compound\
b)\ divide each element's mass by the smallest mass\
c)\ divide every element's moles by the largest mole value\
d)\ round each mole value to the nearest whole number\
e)\ divide every element's moles by the smallest mole value

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**2.** Sucrose has the molecular formula C~12~H~22~O~11~. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ C~6~H~11~O~11~\
b)\ C~12~H~22~O~11~\
c)\ C~12~H~22~O\
d)\ C~6~H~11~O~5~\
e)\ CH~2~O

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**3.** A 2.000 g sample of an iron oxide contains 1.447 g of iron; the rest is oxygen. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Fe~3~O~4~\
b)\ Fe~6~O~8~\
c)\ FeO\
d)\ Fe~3~O\
e)\ FeO~4~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**4.** A white powder is 39.05% K, 1.01% H, 12.00% C, and 47.94% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ K~2~HCO~3~\
b)\ K~39~HC~12~O~47~\
c)\ K~2~H~2~C~2~O~6~\
d)\ K~3~HCO\
e)\ KHCO~3~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```

b)\ C~5~H~10~O~5~\

**7.** A liquid hydrocarbon is 92.26% C and 7.74% H by mass, and its molar mass is 78.11 g/mol. It burns completely in O~2~ to form CO~2~ and H~2~O. How many moles of O~2~ are needed to burn 0.400 mol of the hydrocarbon?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.400 mol\
b)\ 0.500 mol\
c)\ 2.40 mol\
d)\ 3.00 mol\
e)\ 6.00 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**8.** Which statement about the **excess** reactant in a reaction is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ It is used up before the limiting reactant\
b)\ It determines the theoretical yield\
c)\ Its leftover amount is added to the theoretical yield\
d)\ It is always the reactant present in the larger mass\
e)\ Some of it remains unreacted after the reaction stops

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**9.** Octane burns: 2C~8~H~18~(l) + 25O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ 16CO~2~(g) + 18H~2~O(g). How many moles of O~2~ are needed to burn 0.300 mol of C~8~H~18~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.0240 mol\
b)\ 0.300 mol\
c)\ 2.40 mol\
d)\ 3.75 mol\
e)\ 120 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**10.** Mercury(II) oxide decomposes when heated: 2HgO(s) $\rightarrow$ 2Hg(l) + O~2~(g). How many moles of O~2~ form from 21.7 g of HgO?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.0501 mol\
b)\ 0.100 mol\
c)\ 0.200 mol\
d)\ 1.60 mol\
e)\ 4.99 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**11.** The thermite reaction is Fe~2~O~3~(s) + 2Al(s) $\rightarrow$ 2Fe(l) + Al~2~O~3~(s). What mass of Fe forms from 40.0 g of Fe~2~O~3~ with excess Al?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.501 g\
b)\ 6.99 g\
c)\ 14.0 g\
d)\ 28.0 g\
e)\ 80.0 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**12.** Lithium burns according to the **unbalanced** equation Li(s) + O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ Li~2~O(s). What mass of Li~2~O forms from 3.47 g of Li with excess O~2~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.250 g\
b)\ 1.74 g\
c)\ 7.47 g\
d)\ 14.9 g\
e)\ 29.9 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**13.** Silicon carbide forms by SiO~2~(s) + 3C(s) $\rightarrow$ SiC(s) + 2CO(g). A mixture of 30.0 g of SiO~2~ and 15.0 g of C is heated. Which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ C is limiting, and 30.0 g of SiO~2~ is left over\
b)\ C is limiting, and 25.0 g of SiO~2~ is left over\
c)\ C is limiting, and 4.98 g of SiO~2~ is left over\
d)\ Neither is limiting; both reactants are used up completely\
e)\ SiO~2~ is limiting, and C is left over

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**14.** For 3NO~2~(g) + H~2~O(l) $\rightarrow$ 2HNO~3~(aq) + NO(g), 23.0 g of NO~2~ reacts with 5.00 g of H~2~O. What is the theoretical yield of HNO~3~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.333 g\
b)\ 21.0 g\
c)\ 28.0 g\
d)\ 31.5 g\
e)\ 35.0 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**15.** Yeast ferments glucose: C~6~H~12~O~6~(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2C~2~H~5~OH(aq) + 2CO~2~(g). Fermenting 45.0 g of glucose gives 19.5 g of ethanol, C~2~H~5~OH. What is the percent yield?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.847%\
b)\ 43.3%\
c)\ 84.7%\
d)\ 118%\
e)\ 169%

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```
